notes: Sample docker_db_connections.json - the throwaway database containers the SRE app provisions and the drills run against. Copy to docker_db_connections.json and edit.

This file is written BY the tool as much as read by it: 'create-db-docker' registers what it built here, so a lab instance can be found again by anything that needs one. Editing it by hand is fine; expect the tool to add entries.
'id' is the handle every command uses to name one lab instance. 'password_env' names a key in data/encrypted_secret_text.json, never a password.

An empty 'host' means the container runs on the same machine as the process reading this file. 'worker_host' names the machine when it does not - that is how one control node manages labs on several hosts.

'docker.mode' is 'single' for one container, 'ha-lab' for a small cluster ('replicas' says how many). 'compose_path' is where the generated compose file was written on that host, so the cluster can be brought up, down or thrown away without guessing.

Nothing here is production. These are the instances a restore drill restores onto and a version upgrade is rehearsed on - disposable on purpose, which is exactly why the credentials are still kept in the secret store rather than left in the clear.

docker_db_connections._note: The restore target for the drill in restore_config.json. 'database': 'master' because that is what the tool connects to; a restore names its own databases.
